exercises.additional_challenge: Add an Idempotency-Key request header check so retrying a POST request with the same UUID returns the cached response instead of re-executing.

exercises.additional_challenge: Show how a PostgreSQL `MATERIALIZED VIEW` can serve a CQRS read model refreshed via `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY`.
exercises.expected_output: Invarian: Violates Module Table Boundary
exercises.solution_explanation: A simple table-prefix or schema-prefix assertion in unit tests enforces Modular Monolith database boundaries automatically on every commit.
exercises.task_description: Implement ViolatesModuleTableBoundary(moduleName string, referencedTable string) bool that returns true if referencedTable does not start with moduleName + "_".
exercises.title: Enforce Module Table Ownership in a SQL Linter Check

exercises.additional_challenge: Open the Architecture Lab to compare how Layered, Clean, Hexagonal, and Modular Monolith organize these files!
exercises.expected_output:
Invarian: Add Money Same Currency
Invarian: Add Money Rejects Mismatch And Nil
exercises.solution_explanation: Keeping domain invariants in pure functions makes your service architecture clean and prepares you for Lesson 8.1 (Hexagonal Ports & Adapters).
exercises.task_description: Implement AddMoney(a, b *Money) (Money, error) checking if a == nil || b == nil, checking if a.Currency != b.Currency, and returning Money{Cents: a.Cents + b.Cents, Currency: a.Currency}, nil.
exercises.title: Enforce Domain Currency & Nil Invariants in Pure Service Function

exercises.additional_challenge: Write the PostgreSQL query `INSERT INTO processed_events (event_id) VALUES ($1) ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING` to guarantee idempotent message processing.
exercises.expected_output:
Invarian: Circuit Breaker Trips At Threshold
Invarian: Half Open Trips On Single Failure
exercises.solution_explanation: A circuit breaker fails fast while `OPEN`, allows a single probe request after a cooldown window (`HALF_OPEN`), and immediately reverts to `OPEN` if that probe fails.
exercises.task_description: Complete ShouldTripBreaker(consecutiveFailures, threshold int, currentState string) string that transitions a Circuit Breaker from 'CLOSED' or 'HALF_OPEN' to 'OPEN' when consecutiveFailures >= threshold.
exercises.title: Implement an Idempotent Event Consumer Guard & Circuit Breaker State Transition

exercises.additional_challenge: Write an `http.HandlerFunc` for Server-Sent Events (SSE) that checks `flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)` and streams events until `<-r.Context().Done()`.
exercises.expected_output: Invarian: Is Valid W3 C Traceparent
exercises.solution_explanation: The W3C Trace Context specification mandates version `00`, a 16-byte (32 hex char) non-zero `trace-id`, an 8-byte (16 hex char) non-zero `parent-id`, and a 1-byte (2 hex char) `trace-flags` field.
exercises.task_description: Implement IsValidW3CTraceparent(header string) bool that checks whether header splits on '-' into 4 parts where version is '00', traceID is 32 hex chars (not all zeros), and spanID is 16 hex chars.
exercises.title: Validate W3C traceparent Header Format for Distributed Tracing

exercises.additional_challenge: Think about why 100 clients retrying at the exact same 200ms mark still creates spikes, and how adding random jitter smooths the load!
exercises.expected_output:
Invarian: Compute Backoff Ms Progression
Invarian: Compute Backoff Ms Capped At Max
exercises.solution_explanation: Understanding bounded exponential backoff prepares you for Circuit Breakers, Singleflight, and Outbox relays in Lesson 9.1.
exercises.task_description: Implement ComputeBackoffMs(baseMs int64, maxMs int64, attempt int) int64 by clamping attempt < 1 to 1, computing delay := baseMs << (attempt - 1), and capping at maxMs.
exercises.title: Calculate Capped Exponential Backoff Delay Safely
